surface: Secure-element usage (key=se): OPTIGA Trust M V3 + SE050 tunnels, transport→final rotation, PIN-attempt lockstep, lifecycle lockdown, attestation/anti-substitution, wipe paths

improvements.title: Boot-time per-element SE identity pinning (OPTIGA E0C2 UID + E0E0 cert pubkey, SE050 UID/GetVersion OEF) sealed under DHUK at first boot, re-verified before any secret APDU
improvements.threat: Swapped, counterfeit or substituted secure element (supply chain / evil maid / rework after RDP-2): an attacker replaces one SE with a look-alike that answers the tunnel handshake (transport keyset is public at RDP-0) or a re-flashed genuine part, and the firmware cannot tell. Today nothing on the boot path checks which silicon it is talking to.
improvements.proposal: On the first field boot (Phase B, after RDP=0xCC and before the seed wizard) read OPTIGA coprocessor UID (0xE0C2) and the Infineon device-cert public key (0xE0E0, type 0x12 per observed 0xE0E3) over the shield, and SE050 UID + GetVersion/AppletConfig (expect OEF 0xA921 per board/pq1.rs, resolve #697 first); store a DHUK-SAES-CMAC of (UID_O ‖ pk_O ‖ UID_E ‖ cfg_E) in the page-127 journal. On every boot, before `check_provisioned`/`unlock`, re-read both identities and compare per element with FI-double sentinel checks; mismatch on either element is a hard refusal (not a wipe — a fake SE must not be able to trigger the wipe of the real one). Bind each proof to its own element (Trezor's Aug-2026 bug: a combined key set let one proof satisfy all three). Optional second step: a C10-signed MCU attestation over a companion challenge, keyed from a DHUK-derived seed regenerated per use, so a remote verifier gets a one-primitive 'genuine PQ1' proof without any classical signer.
improvements.rationale: Ledger (Genuine Check), Trezor (OPTIGA cert + TROPIC01 pinned pubkey + ML-DSA-44 MCU cert), BitBox02 Nova, Tangem and GridPlus all ship a device-identity check; pq1 ships none and its own docs already claim an 'SE attest' boot step (CLAUDE.md Lifecycle line; HARDENING.md:32, §3.4) that does not exist. Pinning at first boot (when the MCU is already RDP-2 and the attacker has had no window) and checking per element every boot is the cheapest closure of the 'malicious hardware' question for the SE leg; it does not see an implant on the bus (Ledger's stated blind spot) but it does detect the only substitution an implant would need to make to read a half: replacing the chip that holds it. Invariant #5 is respected: OPTIGA/SE050 ECDSA cert chains are only compared as pinned bytes, never used as a signer; the optional MCU attestation is C10.

improvements.title: Die-bind the at-rest SE secrets: SAES(DHUK)-wrap each XOR half before it is stored, and derive both PIN credentials (OPTIGA F1D0 AuthRef secret, SE050 UserID value) through the DHUK KDF so extracting both SE NVMs without this die yields nothing
improvements.threat: Lab extraction of both secure elements' NVM (Donjon's FDTC 2023 double-laser DS28C36 page dump; Tangem S3D232A single-pulse SetPin bypass; TROPIC01 LFI) on a stolen device: today half_O ‖ half_E are stored raw and XOR directly to the BIP-39 entropy, the SE050 UserID *is* the 8-digit PIN, and the OPTIGA AuthRef secret is a public-domain KDF of the PIN — so two extracted chips (or one extracted chip plus a faulted PIN check on the other) reconstruct the seed with no dependence on the STM32 die. The MCU currently adds nothing to the at-rest secrecy floor.
improvements.proposal: Pre-production, no migration needed: (a) in `DualSecureElement::provision` store `wrap_O = SAES_DHUK_CTR(label_O, half_O)` and `wrap_E = SAES_DHUK_CTR(label_E, half_E)` (or equivalently XOR each half with a SAES-CMAC(DHUK, 'pqsigner/half-mask-v1'‖side) keystream — no AEAD needed because the master_secret consistency check at unlock already authenticates the reconstruction) and unwrap in `unlock` after the halves return through the tunnels; (b) replace `derive_pin_secret = kdf("optiga-pin-auth-v1", pin)` with `SAES-CMAC(DHUK, 'pqsigner/optiga-pin-v2' ‖ pin)` and send `SAES-CMAC(DHUK, 'pqsigner/se050-userid-v2' ‖ pin)` (16 B) as the SE050 UserID value instead of the raw PIN; (c) state the resulting floor in threat-model.md: seed recovery needs {OPTIGA NVM, SE050 NVM, this die's DHUK (RDP-2)} or the 24 words. Keep the 3-source TRNG draw and the XOR split unchanged (invariant #1 untouched: neither chip alone reveals any bit, and now neither pair of chips does either).
improvements.rationale: This is the Trezor 'malicious or extracted SE cannot reduce security below the MCU-only design' floor (optiga.md:66, storage.c:633-639) and Coldcard's 'both SE1 and SE2 plus the main micro must be cracked' property, realised with the SAES/DHUK primitive pq1 already uses for PBS derivation — purely symmetric, so it does not re-open the descoped ML-KEM bus wrap (that wrap protected the I2C transit; this protects at rest). Side benefit: the PIN never crosses either I2C bus in any form that is useful off-device, so the accepted Grover-2^64 residual against a captured SCP03 session no longer yields the user's PIN. A fault in one SE's PIN compare (Tangem class) now releases only a DHUK-wrapped half, which is useless without also executing on this die.

Must not be described as re-raising the ML-KEM decision (do not re-raise).

improvements.title: Authenticate wipe-bearing and attempt-bearing SE verdicts: a bare 2-byte SCP03 status word is 'inconclusive', never a wipe or a page-124 charge, until an R-MAC'd probe confirms it
improvements.threat: An unauthenticated I2C interposer (or a glitched bus) forges `0x6986` on CreateSession/VERIFY → `AuthMethodBlocked` → `PinLocked` → one-shot dual-SE wipe with zero attempt budget consumed; or forges `0x6985` so a correct PIN burns a page-124 attempt. Because GP Amd D exempts bare error SWs from R-MAC, the firmware currently treats an unauthenticated byte pair as an authoritative security verdict.
improvements.proposal: In `unwrap_response` tag the n==2 arm's result as `Unauthenticated(sw)`; in `classify_se050_unlock_error` and `authenticate_and_read`, on an unauthenticated 0x6986/0x6985/0x6983 run a confirmation probe that must return a full R-MAC'd response under the same session (e.g. ReadObjectAttributes on a public/admin-readable object, or a GetRandom) and only then promote to `AuthMethodBlocked`; if the probe itself fails bare, classify D1-inconclusive: tear the session down, hard-reset the SE, do not charge page-124, do not wipe, and surface 'SE transport fault' to the user with a bounded retry. Apply the same rule on the OPTIGA side to the globally-mapped statuses that feed wipe verdicts (#120). Count consecutive inconclusive outcomes and escalate to lock (not wipe) after N, so an interposer can only DoS, never destroy.
improvements.rationale: Trezor's rule is 'retry only on errors that prove non-execution, never on ones that may have executed' and Ledger's LSB-016 fix was 'tear the channel down on the first MAC error'; pq1's S-5 P1=0x33 work closed the data path but left the verdict path unauthenticated. A wipe is the most irreversible action the device takes on SE input and is the only one an attacker with just bus access can trigger today. The funds are recoverable from the words, but the brick is permanent on the current SE050 (#168), which makes this a cheap, deniable sabotage primitive.

improvements.title: Runtime SE configuration attestation at every boot: compiled-in expected OPTIGA metadata per OID and SE050 object policy set, read back through the tunnels before any secret is touched, refuse if looser, with a CI-pinned expected table
improvements.threat: A tampered, re-provisioned, factory-skipped or substituted SE whose access conditions are looser than the design (e.g. Read=Always on F1D1, E140 at LcsO<Op after the final rotation, UserID max_attempts raised, write-once policy missing) is silently accepted — the firmware only checks metadata inside the provisioning/lock paths, so a device whose lockdown never happened, or was rolled back on a swapped chip, boots and unlocks normally. This is also the detector for the OP17-1 weak Read AC: today nobody would notice it ratcheted.
improvements.proposal: Add `optiga::audit_metadata()` that, after `ensure_shield`, issues `get_metadata` for F1D0, F1D1..F1D4, F1D8, F1E1, E120, E121, E140 and compares each (via the existing `metadata_matches_expected` / `is_metadata_operational` / `metadata_has_luc_execute` helpers) against a `const EXPECTED_METADATA` table versioned with the lifecycle profile; add `se050::audit_policy()` using ReadIDList + ReadObjectAttributes/CheckObjectExists on every object where the production policy permits the read, plus the GetVersion/AppletConfig assertion. Any 'looser than expected' result is a hard refusal before `check_provisioned`; 'tighter' is accepted. Generate `docs/secure-elements/optiga-expected-metadata.md` from the same table and make `make invariant-gates` diff it (Trezor's docs/core/misc/optiga.md pattern). Record a one-line receipt (expected-table version) in the page-127 journal so a profile upgrade is explicit and journaled.
improvements.rationale: Trezor's `optiga-lock-check`, boot-time `optiga_pin_init_metadata` self-heal and `tropic_ensure_configuration` are the mechanism that turns the S-1/S-2/S-3 lifecycle ceremony from a one-time factory act into a property re-verified on every boot; pq1 fences those ceremonies at compile time only. It directly supports SE-01 (a substituted chip rarely reproduces the exact metadata) and gives S-3 its missing silicon-readable receipt format. Cost is a handful of GetDataObject-metadata reads per boot (tens of ms).

improvements.title: Shielded-Connection liveness probe: after every PRL handshake, send host-TRNG data through the tunnel to a command whose response is a deterministic function of that data (CalcHash) and compare locally — a replayed session cannot answer
improvements.threat: Whole-session replay of a captured OPTIGA unlock session (OP17-2): the Infineon PRL handshake carries only the chip's random_S, so an interposer that recorded one genuine session can replay the chip's frames to the MCU; the vendor-faithful ProVerif model proves inj-agreement false. Combined with a substituted/absent chip this lets a bus device impersonate the OPTIGA for the duration of a session.
improvements.proposal: In `OptigaTrustM::ensure_shield`, immediately after `establish()` succeeds, draw 32 B from `rng_strong`, send OPTIGA `CalcHash(SHA-256, data)` (cmd 0x30, non-counter-bound, no AC) inside the shield, and compare the returned digest against a locally computed SHA-256 (HW HASH) with FI-double sentinel checks; mismatch → `ShieldError::Replay`, tear down, hard-reset, D1-inconclusive classification (no page-124 charge). Because the replayed transcript's CalcHash response was computed over the old data, the compare fails with certainty; the probe costs one APDU (~5 ms). Document the residual honestly: this closes session-level replay by a bus adversary but not an adversary holding the PBS (who can run a real handshake).
improvements.rationale: Trezor has the identical gap (optiga_transport.c:771-780, no master random) and has not closed it; this is a one-APDU 'beyond' fix that needs no change to the chip's protocol, keeps every existing sequence-counter/nonce-wrap guard, and makes #117 falsifiable on the bench (record a session with the LA1010, replay it, assert the probe refuses). It also upgrades the `random()` path: a replayed session would otherwise return recorded TRNG bytes into the 3-source XOR.

improvements.title: Provisioning/first-boot ordering guards: handshake-first E140 write, no plaintext rewrite of a rotated PBS, and fail-SAFE dual is_provisioned with a third (MCU-journal) leg so a transport glitch can never enter the seed wizard on a used device
improvements.threat: (a) `store_objects` step 1 unconditionally writes the current PBS to E140 in plaintext; after the salted-final rotation a wizard re-provision therefore puts the FINAL pairing secret on the I2C bus in clear (OP17-3). (b) SE050 `check_provisioned` fails open (init/transport error → 'unprovisioned'), and dual-SE AND-combines it, so one SE050 glitch on a live device makes the firmware offer the seed wizard, which on confirm overwrites the real wallet's objects (F24). (c) The bench E140 brick (locked at LcsO=Op with an unknown PBS) came from writing E140 without first proving which PBS the chip holds.
improvements.proposal: Port Trezor's sequence 1:1: before any E140 write, attempt a handshake with the expected current PBS; write only if that handshake fails authoritatively (D1 split), never when transport-inconclusive; after writing, prove it with a real handshake before proceeding; refuse the plaintext path entirely once the page-127 journal says `Rotated` (the salted-final PBS may only be installed through `rotate_pbs_to_salted` under the transport shield). Make `Se050::check_provisioned` return `Result<bool>` and map Err → provisioned (fail-safe, matching OPTIGA); add a page-127 'wallet-provisioned' sentinel written after a successful `provision` and require all three (OPTIGA F1E1 ∧ SE050 ∧ journal) to read 'unprovisioned' before the wizard is offered; any disagreement parks with 'SE state mismatch', never wizard. Every provisioning entry point first checks that no later irreversible step (RDP-2 done, rotation done, LcsO=Op) has happened, like Trezor `secrets-init`.
improvements.rationale: These are the exact ordering mistakes Trezor's prodtest guards against (handshake-first E140, refuse secrets-init once locked/paired) and pq1 has already paid for one of them with a bricked bench part. The fail-safe provisioned check is the difference between 'the device parks' and 'the user's funds are overwritten by a wizard misfire'.

improvements.title: Wipe as a verified, redundant, BHK-first transaction: regenerate the page-126 BHK before touching the SEs, Hamming-distant double-checked wipe verdicts, and a boot-time 'wipe verified' assertion that keeps the armed flag until every region and both SEs are confirmed gone
improvements.threat: A wipe (10 wrong PINs, tamper, admin) that is interrupted, glitched or partially executed leaves recoverable state: the SE050 half remains readable under still-valid SCP03 keys, the OPTIGA half survives a failed factory_reset, a single-bool verdict is coerced to 'wiped' (SE17-3), and the next boot has no obligation to finish. Today the page-125 flag covers only the SE050 admin object.
improvements.proposal: (1) Make the first irreversible step of every wipe path the regeneration of the BHK page (fresh 3-source TRNG words into page 126 + TAMP BKP reload) — Trezor's `secret_safety_erase` — so the SE050 SCP03/admin credentials are dead instantly even if the SE delete never runs; then erase page-124/123/127 and run both SE factory resets. (2) Replace plain-bool wipe verdicts with `fi::CfiCounter`-style sentinels with FI-double reads, and treat 'unknown' as 'not wiped' (never coerce). (3) At boot, if the page-125 flag is armed, re-assert: pages 123–127 blank (except flag), OPTIGA F1E1/F1D1 absent via check_exists through the shield, SE050 ENTROPY/USERID absent via CheckObjectExists — only then clear the flag; otherwise resume the wipe. (4) Include the duress object set (F1D8/E121, DURESS_*) in the wipe list so decoys do not survive. (5) Record one receipt line in the journal so a forensic read shows 'wiped at boot N'.
improvements.rationale: Ledger's 1.4 fix made the user-zone wipe 'verified at startup'; Trezor's BHK regeneration gives a single atomic action that invalidates every BHK-wrapped secret regardless of what happens afterwards. pq1 already owns the BHK axis for SE050 (owner decision 2026-09-21) so the BHK-first step costs one page program and immediately strengthens the 10-wrong-PIN brick and the tamp-wipe path against power-cut and glitch interruption.

improvements.title: Lifetime, unresettable OPTIGA usage budget on the half_O read path (E122, Change=Never) plus Security-Event-Counter (E0C5) awareness so counter-reset bugs and throttling are bounded and visible
improvements.threat: Any bug or fault that resets E120 / page-124 (the E120 reset already runs after every success and on admin wipe; F25 shows it also ratchets on successes) converts the OPTIGA into an unbounded PIN-guessing oracle; separately, repeated failed AUTOREF verifies raise the chip's SEC and the resulting throttling (>127 → up to 5 s/command) is currently indistinguishable from a transport wedge, which under OP17-4 burns page-124 toward self-wipe.
improvements.proposal: (a) Provision E122 as a monotonic LUC with Change=Never after init (limit sized for the device lifetime, e.g. 200,000 — ~20 years at 25 unlocks/day) and add `&& LUC(E122)` to the Read AC of F1D1 (half_O) and F1D2 (master) so every release of the half consumes one unit of a budget no code path can reset; park the device with 'lifetime budget exhausted — restore from words' when it hits the limit. (b) Read E0C5 at boot and before unlock, size the PRL timeouts from it, log it in the journal, and classify 'SEC high' as inconclusive-throttled rather than tamper. (c) Expose E122 remaining and SEC via CMD_GET_REMAINING-adjacent read-only status (non-secret).
improvements.rationale: Trezor's PIN_TOTAL_CTR (E121, 600,000, Change=Never) exists precisely to make 'attacker found a counter-reset bug' a bounded loss; pq1 has only E120 (resettable) and E121 (duress). E122/E123 are free on this chip and the command path (`provision_counter`/UPCTR metadata) already exists. SEC handling is a same-chip operational lesson that avoids misclassifying throttling as an attack.

improvements.title: Measurement-bound SE release (DICE-style): the FSBL hands a DHUK-sealed digest of the verified active slot to the secure world, and the OPTIGA/SE050 PIN credentials are derived from PIN ‖ that digest, so a modified secure image cannot obtain either half even after a full MCU compromise
improvements.threat: Donjon's Safe 3 result: SE pairing-secret possession proves 'access to a secret, not the software running on the microcontroller'; a glitched RDP downgrade or any code execution on the die recomputes DHUK-derived pairing/SCP03 keys and uses the SEs as an unlock oracle (with the PIN). pq1's FSBL fingerprint is a human-checked indicator; nothing cryptographic stops a wrong image from talking to the SEs once it runs in the secure world.
improvements.proposal: In the WRP-protected FSBL (before RDP-2 freezes it, i.e. part of the shipping image, not a runtime write): after verifying the active slot hash H, compute M = SAES-CMAC(DHUK, 'pqsigner/boot-measure-v1' ‖ H) and leave M in a TAMP backup register pair that the FSBL then write-locks for the boot (or in a secure-SRAM mailbox the secure image consumes and zeroizes). The secure world folds M into the SE-02 credential KDFs: OPTIGA AuthRef secret = SAES-CMAC(DHUK, PIN ‖ M), SE050 UserID = SAES-CMAC(DHUK, PIN ‖ M). An image with a different H derives wrong credentials → both SEs refuse → attempts are consumed, nothing is released. A legitimate firmware update becomes a journaled credential migration run by the OLD image before reboot (re-provision F1D0 and re-key the UserID under the new H, Trezor-style idempotent/resumable), extending the existing page-127 journal and the authenticate-before-rotate proof object.
improvements.rationale: This is Tillitis' CDI = H(UDS, app) binding and Trezor's 'bootloader decides which SE credentials the next stage may see' (vtrust/secret_prepare_fw), realised with pq1's existing primitives (FSBL measurement, SAES-DHUK, TAMP BKP latch already proven for BHK). It turns invariant #10's boot-time fingerprint from an indicator into a cryptographic gate enforced by the SEs themselves, which is the strongest available answer to 'malicious firmware/hardware on the MCU side' short of a certified SE running the wallet. It is the one item here that would put pq1 beyond both Ledger and Trezor on this surface.

improvements.risks: FSBL flash/stack budget is the known NO-GO class (A/B rollback review) — adds a SAES-CMAC and a BKP write to a 40 KiB frozen region that cannot be patched after RDP-2, so it must be right the first time and FI-hardened (F15); every firmware update now carries a credential migration that can brick on power cut (journal + authenticate-before-rotate + silicon receipts required, same gate set as #268/#76); the BKP handoff register must be unreadable/unwritable by later S-world code or NS (TAMP secure-zone config #50 is a prerequisite); does not help if the FSBL itself is glitched into accepting a bad hash (F15 remains the floor); explicitly NOT a runtime write to the FSBL range.

improvements.title: User-contributed entropy phase in the seed wizard (dice/coin/key-press rolls) mixed into the 3-source TRNG draw, with an on-screen proof that the user's input changed the words
improvements.threat: A backdoored or mis-configured entropy path at seed generation that every on-device check passes (Coldcard 2021–2026: PRNG fallback + 32-bit reseed survived its health checks; #704 shows pq1's TRNG runs RM0456 configuration C, not the certifiable A): all three XOR'd sources sit behind firmware the user cannot audit at runtime, and a factory/pre-power image that fixes the output is invisible to the SWD verify if it lives in a rotated slot.
improvements.proposal: Insert a mandatory wizard step between PIN set and `rng_strong::fill`: the user enters ≥50 dice rolls (or 128 coin flips / 65 key presses, Coldcard's thresholds) on the two-button UI; firmware computes `entropy = rng_strong(32) XOR SHA-256('pqsigner/user-entropy-v1' ‖ rolls)` and, before showing the 24 words, shows a 2-word 'entropy check' derived from `SHA-256(rolls)` that the user can recompute offline (documented procedure), proving the rolls were consumed. Keep the strict 3-source draw unchanged; the user term is an additional XOR share. Allow a documented 'skip' only in bench builds.
improvements.rationale: After the Coldcard incident, user-manipulated entropy is the one defence that provably held when the device's own RNG failed; NGRAVE and Coldcard ship it. pq1 already does the vendor-side part (STM32 ⊕ OPTIGA ⊕ SE050, Cypherock/Trezor parity) so the delta is small and purely additive. It also partially answers 'what if the factory image was swapped before my SWD check' for the seed itself.
